deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous pages: X is a space with a 'global stratification' indexed by a poset I. It is given by closed pieces X_i, with X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k, and i(x) is the least index whose piece contains x. Page 54 defines Ẋ_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j (closed in X_i) and X_i^* = X_i \ Ẋ_i (open in X_i). It proves that the X_i^* partition X.

Grothendieck also uses a (semi-)simplicial space X_{Δ_•}. Its definition is not on these pages, but it is presumably X_{Δ_r} = ∐ over chains i_0 ≤ … ≤ i_r of X_{i_0}, a nerve-type construction over the poset. The map σ_r : X_{Δ_r} → X_{Δ_0} comes from the vertex-0 inclusion Δ_0 → Δ_r. He sets Ẋ_{Δ_0} = ∐ Ẋ_i and X^*_{Δ_0} = ∐ X_i^*, and pulls both back along σ_r to get Ẋ_{Δ_r} (closed) and X^*_{Δ_r} (open, its complement).

This page, formula (29): if α : Δ_{r'} → Δ_r preserves the vertex 0, then α^* : X_{Δ_r} → X_{Δ_{r'}} satisfies σ_{r'} ∘ α^* = σ_r. Hence α^* pulls X^*_{Δ_{r'}} back to X^*_{Δ_r}, equivalently Ẋ_{Δ_{r'}} back to Ẋ_{Δ_r}.

NB (read as 'Moralement'): X^*_{Δ_r} is a kind of 'non-singular' part of X_{Δ_r}, and Ẋ_{Δ_r} is the singular part, or 'boundary'. One must note that the X^*_{Δ_r} do not form a semi-simplicial space. Only the operators fixing 0 preserve them; for example the face d_0 does not.

Nevertheless the aim, 'in a suitable context', is to reconstitute X from its open strata X_i^*. This follows the spirit of §1, the two-strata case: X_0 = Y closed in X_1 = X, with Y^* = Y and X^* = X \ Y. There one had to introduce U_{Y,X}, the deleted tubular neighbourhood. The next page (§3, 'introduction aux tubes') carries this out with tubular neighbourhoods V̄_{i,j} of X_i in X_j and their 'boundaries'.

In modern terms, this is the start of describing a poset-stratified space by its strata together with gluing data (tubes or links) indexed by chains in the poset. Such data is a functor on the subdivision sd(I) (chains), i.e. the program of reconstructing a stratified space or homotopy type from strata plus links.
errors: As written, formula (29) reads α^*(X^*_{Δ_{r'}}) = X^*_{Δ_r}, which has the wrong variance, since α^* goes from X_{Δ_r} to X_{Δ_{r'}}. The intended statement is surely (α^*)^{-1}(X^*_{Δ_{r'}}) = X^*_{Δ_r}, with the same for Ẋ. It follows at once from σ_{r'} ∘ α^* = σ_r when α(0) = 0.
The proof of the Proposition on the previous page is somewhat garbled ('X_j^* = X_j \ X_i^*' should read X_j \ Ẋ_j), but the statement is correct.

ideas.what: Simplicial space over the chains of the stratification poset, with open/closed ('regular'/'boundary') parts pulled back along the vertex-0 map. These parts are stable only under operators fixing 0, so they do not form a semi-simplicial space.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of strata/links over sd(P); décalage-type sub-object stable under 0-preserving maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stratified homotopy theory: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988), MacPherson/Treumann/Lurie (exit paths), Douteau, Haine, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Program of reconstituting a stratified space from its open strata and tubular-neighbourhood data, generalising the two-strata case with the deleted tube U_{Y,X}.
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction from strata + links / tubular neighbourhoods (control data, décollement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (control data), Quinn, Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 on tame topology and the 'dévissage' of stratified structures via tubular neighbourhoods

deep.surprise_reason: This is a transitional, motivational page: a routine compatibility check, a remark that the open parts are not semi-simplicial, and a restatement of the programme announced in the Esquisse. It contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'On ferait attention que les X^*_{Δr} un fermé par un espace semi-simplicial' should be 'On fera attention que les X^*_{Δr} ne forment pas un espace semi-simplicial'.
'dans un contexte[?] [?]' is probably 'dans un contexte convenable'.
